# Purpose

`scripts/sales_summary.R` summarizes one month of (synthetic) retail order
data for a small coffee-and-goods shop. It answers a single business
question — **which product category drives the most revenue?** — by
computing total revenue, per-category revenue, order counts, and average
order value, then saving a summary table and a bar chart.

## Inputs

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `data/retail_orders.csv` | 60 synthetic orders for September 2026. Columns: `order_id`, `order_date`, `category` (Coffee / Tea / Pastries / Merchandise), `quantity`, `unit_price`, `region`. |

```{r load-data}
orders <- read.csv("data/retail_orders.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
orders$order_date <- as.Date(orders$order_date)
str(orders)
```

## Outputs

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `output/category_summary.csv` | Revenue, order count, and average order value per category, sorted highest revenue first. |
| `output/revenue_by_category.png` | Bar chart of revenue by category. |

The script also prints total revenue and the top-performing category to the
console.

# Walkthrough

### 1. Compute each order's line total

```{r line-total}
orders$line_total <- orders$quantity * orders$unit_price
total_revenue <- sum(orders$line_total)
sprintf("Total revenue: $%.2f across %d orders", total_revenue, nrow(orders))
```

### 2. Aggregate by category

```{r aggregate}
category_summary <- aggregate(
  line_total ~ category, data = orders,
  FUN = function(x) c(revenue = sum(x), orders = length(x), avg_order = mean(x))
)
category_summary <- do.call(data.frame, category_summary)
names(category_summary) <- c("category", "revenue", "orders", "avg_order_value")
category_summary$revenue <- round(category_summary$revenue, 2)
category_summary$avg_order_value <- round(category_summary$avg_order_value, 2)
category_summary <- category_summary[order(-category_summary$revenue), ]
knitr::kable(category_summary, row.names = FALSE)
```

### 3. Identify the top category

```{r top-category}
sprintf("Top-performing category: %s ($%.2f)",
        category_summary$category[1], category_summary$revenue[1])
```

### 4. Chart

```{r chart, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
bp <- barplot(
  category_summary$revenue,
  names.arg = category_summary$category,
  col = "#1F4E78", border = NA,
  main = "September 2026 Revenue by Category",
  ylab = "Revenue ($)",
  ylim = c(0, max(category_summary$revenue) * 1.15)
)
text(bp, category_summary$revenue,
     labels = sprintf("$%.0f", category_summary$revenue),
     pos = 3, cex = 0.9)
```
